title: Counting obstruction to low-degree approximation on the root cube
statement: Let $K$ be a finite field, fix an element $\omega \in K$, and let $n, D, e, B$ be natural numbers. Write $\{1,\omega\}^n$ for the cube of vectors in $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$ whose every coordinate equals $1$ or $\omega$. Suppose a finite index set $\mathrm{Cand}$ is equipped with a map assigning to each candidate $c$ a polynomial $P_c \in K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, and that the following hold: (i) every polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $D$ agrees, at every point of $\{1,\omega\}^n$, with $P_c$ for some candidate $c$; (ii) for each candidate $c$, the Hamming ball of radius $e$ centered at the function $x \mapsto P_c(x)$ contains at most $B$ functions $\{1,\omega\}^n \to K$; and (iii) $\abs{\{1,\omega\}^n \to K} > \abs{\mathrm{Cand}}\cdot B$. Then it is not the case that every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ admits a polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $D$ differing from $f$ on at most $e$ points of the cube.
hypotheses_covered: a distinguished element ω of K
natural numbers n, D, e, B
a finite candidate type Cand with a polynomial-valued map poly
completeness: every total-degree-≤D polynomial agrees on the cube with some poly c
ball bound: each candidate's evaluation function has a radius-e Hamming ball of size ≤ B
strict counting: |functions on the cube → K| > |Cand| · B
replaced:
Suppose a finite family $(\mathrm{poly}\,c)_{c \in \mathrm{Cand}}$ represents, on the cube,
every polynomial of total degree at most $D$; suppose each Hamming ball of radius $e$
around such a candidate has at most $B$ elements; and suppose
$\abs{\{1,\omega\}^n \to K} > \abs{\mathrm{Cand}} \cdot B$. Then it is not the case that
every function on the cube has a degree-$\le D$ approximant with at most $e$ bad points.
